price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: defensive suppression (a suppressed play type followed by a recommended counter mix)
suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix (BEST vs AVOID counters)
adherence/conformance of observed mix to recommended mix
methodological_questions: Does adherence to the recommended mix predict winning after controlling for team and opponent quality?
Is the recommended mix derived out of sample, or from outcomes that also define winning?
Is the sample of about 54 series enough for a series-level test?
Are play-type labels and adherence measures reliable, and are they free of mechanical floors?
Are the recommendations stable across seasons and between population, team and matchup levels?

historical_evidence.finding: A series-level AVOID share vs winning test with n=50 series gave rho=-0.26, p=0.07, and the record states it was underpowered (about 80 series needed for p<0.05). The game-level rho=-0.19, p=0.008 used inflated n and was confounded by team quality. The record says it was still confounded (OKC disciplined and good). Verdict: inconclusive.

In holdout games, closer alignment to the recommended mix gave higher ORtg (raw gap +5.18, strength-controlled +3.27 ORtg; PPP residual +0.0193 vs -0.0134). This was efficiency, not winning, and the validation was recorded as same-pipeline. n=908 team-game rows with no CI. Model regret is non-negative by construction.
Descriptive BEST/AVOID shares by team. Win% was not identified with BEST share (IND 4.5% BEST, 71% win; ORL 59.3% AVOID, 0% win). There was no inferential stability test, and the sample was 19 teams.

Matchup-specific non-CUT BEST counters did not beat a constrained league mix (gap +0.010, p=0.171, n=136; L3 non-CUT +0.001, p=0.328, n=47). The headline BEST-vs-mix gap was CUT-driven. The record cites selection/regression to the mean and small sample as limits.

Conformance of observed mix to the recommended opener was measured on 4 playoff G1 games. Average |delta| was 4.5 to 24.0pp, and 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. CUT and PNR were muted by the tagger floor. There was no outcome comparison.

The best counter is not clearly stable across population, team and matchup levels (for example MIA team-level disagrees with population on DRIVE). Matchup cells are small (n_mu 5 to 696; playoff matchups 4 to 44).

The play-type label audit failed overall: OTHER was 20.2% against a target below 10%, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, and DRIVE foul-draw was 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark. The record says label issues undermine adaptation findings.
An assisted-flag leak (the flag exists only on makes) produced SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP. After the rewrite they were about 1.16 and 1.20.

Stacked suppression effects were less than additive (-0.071 vs -0.232 predicted), and the record lists an implementation bug and small samples as limits. This bears on the stability of suppression-conditional effects.
Defensive scheme labels were available for only 3.3% to 14.9% of possessions, and switches_on was unpopulated. Suppression defined by scheme is therefore hard to measure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level test of play-type mix discipline (AVOID share) against winning
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: small sample (n=50, about 80 needed) and team-quality confound. Game-level significance was inflated by non-independence.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Claiming matchup-specific BEST counters add value beyond a league mix
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a powered null once CUT was excluded. The headline gap was CUT-driven, with selection/regression-to-the-mean and small-sample limits.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred play-type labels as the basis for adaptation findings
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a label audit failure (C_artifact): high OTHER share, low-confidence labels, foul possessions leaking into OTHER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Early possession-level play-type PPP from the classifier
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: assisted flag exists only on makes, which inflated SPOT_UP PPP.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using single-game conformance to the recommended opener as an outcome-linked measure
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits: mechanical floor (CUT/PNR muted by tagger), single-game horizon, no outcome comparison.

evidence_establishes: Per FAM:SF-APPM-001, on a same-pipeline holdout, closer alignment to the recommended mix went with higher efficiency, and this survived team/opponent residualization (+3.27 ORtg).
Per FAM:SF-CHT-039, a series-level mix-discipline vs winning association was borderline (rho=-0.26, p=0.07, n=50) and confounded by team quality. About 80 series were stated to be needed.
Per FAM:SF08, win% was not identified with BEST share in descriptive team-level data.
Per FAM:SF-APPS-023, the non-CUT matchup-specific advantage was null (n=136).
Per FAM:SF-APPM-014 and FAM:SF-PAP-096, play-type labels have recorded reliability and artifact problems.
evidence_does_not_establish: That adherence predicts winning, whether at game or series level, after controlling for team quality.
That the recommended mix was derived out of sample with respect to the series being predicted.
That the efficiency link in FAM:SF-APPM-001 carries over to wins. That study used the same pipeline, and its regret is non-negative by construction.
That adherence is measured reliably across all play types, given the label audit failure and tagger floors.
That the answer would change with 54 series rather than 50, since the stated requirement was about 80.
own_inferences: With 54 series (barely above the 50 in FAM:SF-CHT-039), a series-level test has only a borderline effect (rho about 0.26) and is still underpowered. It cannot support a confirmatory claim at alpha 0.05.
A game-level test clustered by series, with team-strength controls, can have more usable power but is exposed to confounding and to outcome-derived recommendations.

Efficiency alignment (+3.27 ORtg) is probably mediated by shot quality and by game state (leading teams alter their mix). Reverse causation (winning teams get to run preferred plays) is therefore a serious alternative explanation for any adherence-win association.
Because the CUT-driven headline gap disappears for non-CUT plays, an adherence index dominated by CUT may be driven by a mechanical or label effect rather than by a strategy effect.
The question as posed is vague on the adherence metric, the recommendation source and the level of analysis, so it is not pre-registerable without those specifications.
uncertainties: Whether the 54 series include partial 2025-26 playoff series (the playoffs are complete only from 2026-06-21) and how many are regular-season or play-in units.
How the recommended mix is derived (population, team or matchup level) and whether it was fit on data that include the test series.
Whether the earlier n=50 series sample overlaps with the 54, in which case the added evidence is nearly nil.
Whether play-type labels have been repaired since the FAM:SF-APPM-014 audit.
The exact definition of the suppression trigger and the adherence metric, which the records do not fully specify.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history, a straightforward proceed on 54 series would look reasonable. FAM:SF-CHT-039 shows the series-level version was already underpowered and confounded at n=50 with about 80 needed. FAM:SF-APPS-023 shows the matchup-specific advantage is null beyond CUT, FAM:SF-APPM-001 shows the supportive efficiency result used a same-pipeline validation, and the label audit failures add a measurement risk. Together these moved the decision from proceed to proceed_with_changes: only a restricted, exploratory-labelled, game-level clustered design with a frozen out-of-sample recommender, with no confirmatory series-level claim.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series is below the roughly 80 that FAM:SF-CHT-039 stated were needed for a borderline effect (rho about -0.26).
Team quality, opponent strength and game state drive both adherence and winning, and the prior series-level test was still confounded.
If the recommended mix is derived from outcomes (PPP/results) that overlap the test games, adherence is mechanically related to winning (regret is non-negative by construction in FAM:SF-APPM-001).
The play-type label audit failed (FAM:SF-APPM-014), so adherence measured on those labels is unreliable.

prior_work.summary: Adherence has been linked to efficiency (FAM:SF-APPM-001, supported, same-pipeline validation). A series-level mix-discipline vs winning test was inconclusive and underpowered (FAM:SF-CHT-039). Descriptive team-level data did not link BEST share to wins (FAM:SF08). The matchup-specific non-CUT advantage was a powered null (FAM:SF-APPS-023). No retrieved record tests adherence to the recommended mix against winning with an out-of-sample recommender and team-quality control, so the question as posed is only partly answered.

risks.text: 54 series gives low power for a rho of about 0.2 to 0.3, and the prior n=50 test was p=0.07. Game-level n is inflated by within-series dependence.
Talent and opponent quality drive both mix discipline and wins (the OKC example). Game state also drives mix (reverse causality).
Recommendations derived from PPP/outcomes in the same sample make adherence correlate with winning by construction.
If the recommender, suppression triggers or leverage weights are fit on games that include the evaluated series or later games, the test leaks.
Play-type labels failed the audit (OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence), and foul possessions leak into OTHER.
CUT and PNR are muted by the tagger floor, and the CUT-driven headline gap can dominate the adherence index.
Post-suppression possessions with a defined BEST/AVOID recommendation are sparse per series. SF08 shows a team with 70.8% INSUFF, and matchup cells have n as small as 4 to 5.
Recommendations may not be stable across seasons and between population, team and matchup levels (FAM:SF08, FAM:SF-APPM-055).
Many play types, trigger types, adherence metrics and levels make forking paths likely unless the metric and level are fixed in advance.
Teams or series selected for extreme adherence will regress toward the mean, and the playoff sample is selected on team quality.

design.estimand: Within-series game-level association between a team's adherence (negative leverage-weighted L1 distance between observed post-suppression mix and the recommended mix) and winning that game, conditional on pre-game team strength difference. Reported as an odds ratio per 1 SD of adherence, with a series-level secondary association only as exploratory.
design.unit: Team-game, clustered by series (and by team-season). Series-level analysis is secondary and descriptive only.
design.sample: All games in the 54 available series from 2022-23 to 2025-26 playoffs, excluding garbage-time and blowout possessions. The recommender is frozen before looking at outcomes, fit only on regular-season data and prior seasons. The 2025-26 playoff data are treated as the confirmatory holdout once complete (from 2026-06-21). Games with too few post-suppression possessions are excluded by a pre-set rule, and the exclusion count is reported.
design.power: Series-level: with n=54 and rho of about 0.26, power is roughly 0.5 to 0.55 at alpha 0.05, so a result there is not confirmatory. FAM:SF-CHT-039 stated about 80 series are needed. Game-level: compute power by simulation using the cluster-robust ICC and the observed number of games per series, and pre-register the minimum detectable odds ratio. If it exceeds a plausible effect, label the study exploratory.
design.controls: Pre-game strength (net rating or Elo-style rating from prior games only), opponent strength, home court, series fixed effects, and in-game score margin and leverage (exclude possessions after the outcome is effectively decided). Adherence is computed on non-CUT plays separately, given the CUT-driven gap in FAM:SF-APPS-023. Include label-confidence filtering based on FAM:SF-APPM-014, and run a sensitivity check excluding OTHER.
design.falsification: Placebo tests: (1) adherence to a shuffled or other-opponent recommended mix should not predict winning; (2) adherence to a league-default mix should be compared as a baseline, and the recommender must add information beyond it; (3) a negative-control outcome (the previous game's result) should show no association; (4) check that the effect survives dropping CUT and conditioning on shot quality, to check it is not mediated purely by game state.
design.multiplicity: One primary metric (all-play-type adherence at the population level) and one primary model. Team-level and matchup-level recommenders and per-play-type breakdowns are secondary, with Holm correction across at most 6 pre-listed secondary tests.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the cluster-robust primary odds ratio is above 1 with a 95% CI excluding 1 in the 2025-26 holdout and a same-direction estimate in the earlier seasons, and the effect survives the placebo and non-CUT checks. Rejected if the CI excludes the minimum effect of interest and power was adequate. Otherwise report inconclusive, and do not claim a series-level result below about 80 series.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and the derived play-type graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26. Freeze a snapshot with the date, label/tagger version and recommender version. The 2025-26 playoff holdout is analysed only after the complete data are available (2026-06-21 or later).

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix predict game or series wins out of sample?
How is the recommended mix derived and is it computed from outcomes that also define winning (outcome-derived label, leakage)?
Is a sample of 54 series sufficient for power given exposure sparsity of suppression conditions?
How should confounding by team quality and opponent strength be handled?
Are suppression-conditional recommendations stable across seasons (drift) and reliable?
args.query: adherence to suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix predicts winning; best/avoid counter strategy against defensive suppression; series-level evaluation

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull the full SF-CHT-039 record or just wrap up, and since the record already looks fairly complete, I'll finish without another tool call. The core question is whether adhering to the suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning across 54 series, and the prior study on 50 series showed a weak negative correlation (rho=-0.26, p=0.07).

I'm checking the series count against the playoff schedule: the 2025-26 playoffs only partly finished by the time the question was posed, so the 54 series are probably a partial set. The other studies hold up poorly here too: the efficiency result doesn't carry over to winning, the non-CUT comparison is a null, and the label audit failed. Leaning toward proceeding with changes, though I expect the testable signal to be small.

I'm settling the status labels for each study: the efficiency result is supported, the non-CUT comparison and the label audit don't hold, and several others are untestable or just not hypothesis tests. I'm also estimating how likely each outcome is, and putting the testable chance around 0.2 with the rest split across artifact, uncertain, and the other buckets.
